podcast.body: During the presentation of *The King of Limbs*, Thom Yorke and Stan Lee Donwood were photographed together distributing free newspapers in the street. This public appearance was crucial in officially debunking the long-standing rumor that Donwood was merely a pseudonym for Yorke. "repartido periódicos gratuitos en la calle cuando presentarán el King of Limes. Era una de las fotos que desmintió oficialmente que Thom Yorke y Stan Lee Donwood no eran la misma persona."

podcast.body: This album, the band's eighth, was conceived primarily in a studio setting, contrasting with the road-tested approach of its predecessor, "In Rainbows." Recording spanned almost two years, largely taking place in Los Angeles, with rumors of a temporary studio set up at actress Drew Barrymore's home, which was cryptically acknowledged in the liner notes. The album featured extensive use of samples, loops, ambient sounds, and complex edits, centering its sound around the rhythm section of bassist Colin Greenwood and drummer Phil Selway, and even incorporated turntables with vinyl emulation software. Announced on February 14, 2011, on the band's website, it was made available digitally five days later, with MP3s priced at $9 US and WAV files at $14 US; physical versions were released in May. At 37 minutes, it was their shortest album. Its release was accompanied by the "Newspaper edition," a collaboration with Stanley Donwood, featuring a newspaper-like insert designed to fade in sunlight as a metaphor for natural decay, and distributed as a free paper called "Universal Sigh" at indie record stores globally on March 28, 2011, containing poetry, lyrics, artwork, and short stories. "At 37 minutes, this was the shortest radiohead album to date."
